A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RL-RC-DoT. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial changes in layout and numbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original compression experiments on BDD100K, including detection, ROI encoding, task/model transfer, component ablations and action-resolution analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds DAVIS segmentation, tracking, cross-preset evaluation and quantization-map analysis.

M1.justification: The encoder-statistics inputs, PPO policy, block-level QP actions, action-space coarsening, task/bit-rate reward and auxiliary reward-prediction loss are unchanged. The appendix architecture and loss weights also match; the new evaluations do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates BDD100K detection, saliency-based ROI encoding and transfer to another detector and car segmentation. V2 retains this coverage and adds DAVIS video object segmentation and detection-to-multi-object-tracking evaluation in Appendix 7.3.1, substantially extending the represented data and task requirements.

E2.justification: X264 remains the compression comparator throughout. The newly introduced Mask R-CNN and ByteTracker are downstream evaluators, and Eigen-CAM supplies reference maps; they are not competing compression methods. The x264 preset sweep changes settings, not comparator membership.

E3.justification: The original splits, resizing, bit-rate range and training budget remain unchanged. Added studies introduce Mask R-CNN/IoU, ByteTracker/MOTA, evaluation of the medium-trained policy under other x264 presets, and normalized-map KL divergence. These extend the evaluation settings. The map reference is called Eigen-CAM in the text but grad-CAM on Figure 11's axis.

E4.justification: V2 retains the component ablations, action-resolution analysis and earlier task/model transfer tests. It substantially expands analysis with detector-map alignment in Section 5.2 and Appendix 7.3.3, generalization across x264 presets in Appendix 7.3.2, and detection-to-tracking transfer in Appendix 7.3.1.

E5.justification: Matched tables retain their uncertainty reporting, including Table 1's mean and s.e.m. across test frames. No new seed counts, repeated-run procedures, confidence intervals or significance tests are specified. The added task and preset results are point estimates without new uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables and performance plots retain their results. V2 adds reported BD-rate savings of 8% on DAVIS and 3.2% for tracking, preset-specific scores such as -14.5 for superfast and -25.2 for slow, and mean KL divergence of 2.6 versus x264's 4.4. Table 9's fast-preset entry is printed as '-22/8' and cannot reliably be interpreted.

T1.justification: The MDP definition, discounted-return objective and task/bit-rate reward equations remain mathematically equivalent. The RD/BD-rate explanation is moved to Appendix 7.2. No new theorem, proof, derivation or formal property is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims: task-aware compression over standard encoders, no downstream-task execution during inference, block-level control, auxiliary reward prediction and transfer across related models/tasks. The added experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new map analysis as evidence that bit allocation favors regions informative for detection. Its conclusion also explains that H.265/H.266 deployment would require encoder-specific adaptations, such as CTU features, and proposes unsupervised reward metrics for generalization. The previous training-cost and resolution limitations remain.

D1.justification: V1 reports approximately 50 FPS during training and 30 FPS during evaluation. V2 replaces this discussion with agent-only timing of 0.004 seconds, or 250 FPS, explicitly additional to encoder time; this is not a comparable speedup. Hardware, eight parallel environments, 20 million training frames and four days of training are retained in Appendix 7.7.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Mask R-CNN, Eigen-CAM, DAVIS and ByteTrack to support its new evaluations. The related-work discussion and positioning against previous task-aware and RL-based compression approaches remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. V2 edits block terminology, author affiliations and the conclusion's opening, groups environment and architecture details under Appendix 7.1, moves the RD/BD-rate background into Appendix 7.2, and adds subsections for the new analyses. This is limited editing and reorganization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the manuscript, resizing and repositioning figures and tables, using side captions for several main-text displays, and bringing appendix discussions together with their figures. It adds the QP-map comparison in Figure 4, KL-distribution plot in Figure 11 and preset comparison in Table 9. Existing displays are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for generalization through DAVIS segmentation, tracking transfer and cross-preset tests, and adds evidence connecting bit allocation to detector-relevant regions. These are useful gains while the method and original results remain stable. Their strength is limited by brief new-task protocols, absent uncertainty estimates for the new scores, the malformed fast-preset entry and the Eigen-CAM/grad-CAM labeling inconsistency. Agent-only timing clarifies overhead but replaces the earlier training/evaluation throughput information.
